shared_elements: circle/disc motif (round boss on A, chariot wheel on B)
low-relief carving of figures on a stone surface
justification: The only overlap is generic: both surfaces show a human form and a prominent circular element (a round boss on the statue's body versus a spoked chariot wheel), things any tradition could produce independently. A is a single frontal, massively schematic, near-symmetrical figure with abstract chest and belt motifs, while B is a multi-figure narrative profile scene of a horse-drawn chariot with rider, attendant and a trampled fallen man — different subject, different viewpoint convention, no shared relationships or layout.
